newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel troops wound three Arabs in Hebron clashes.
newsitem.headline: Israel troops wound three Arabs in Hebron clashes.

text.p: Israeli troops wounded three Palestinians in clashes with stone-throwing Arab demonstrators in the West Bank town of Hebron on Sunday, witnesses and hospital officials said.
The clashes broke out for the second straight day on the border between Palestinian-controlled parts of Hebron and Jewish enclaves in the centre of the city which are guarded by Israeli troops.
Witnesses said some 150 protesters hurling stones and firebombs clashed with Israeli troops in the narrow streets of Hebron -- home to around 100,000 Palestinians -- for more than two hours.
Israeli soldiers firing rubber bullets slightly wounded three protesters, officials at Hebron's Alia hospital said.
"How can we have peace here when soldiers must fire on everyone?" one demonstrator told an Israel Radio reporter on the scene.
The radio said an Israeli border policeman was slightly injured when a demonstrator armed with a slingshot hurled a marble into his eye.
Witnesses said Palestinian police did not intervene to disperse demonstrators.

They said Israel had substantially beefed up its forces near the heavily fortified enclaves that are home to 400 Jewish settlers following heavier clashes on Saturday when 30 Palestinians were wounded.
Israel handed 80 percent of Hebron to Palestinian rule in January under an interim peace deal but kept troops to protect the settler enclaves in the town.
Tensions between Israel and the Palestinians have been high since Israel began building a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem in March, plunging peacemaking into deep crisis.
Palestinians, who want East Jerusalem as capital of a future satte, say settlement building in Jerusalem pre-empts final peace talks on the city's fate.
Israel vows never to cede any part of the city. It captured East Jerusalem in the 1967 Middle East war and, in a move unrecognised by the international community, annexed it.
